chunks: ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the obligatory ẓihār. He said:
It is that by which a man intends ẓihār itself specifically.

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the husband or man making the statement
key_terms.الظِّهَارِ: Ẓihār, the formula by which a wife is likened in prohibition to a forbidden relative
key_terms.الْوَاجِبِ: legally binding or operative in ruling
key_terms.بِعَيْنِهِ: specifically, in its very sense, explicitly as such

ai.seo_question: When does ẓihār become legally binding in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal criterion for when ẓihār is considered binding. It indicates that the ruling applies when a man specifically intends the utterance as ẓihār itself, making intention central to the legal effect of the statement.
